summary: The note describes a student entrepreneurship program launched at New Horizons Academy in September 2023, led by educator Sarah Johnson and mentor Robert Li. It covers curriculum changes, pitch coaching, local business partnerships, the Enterprise Connect community network, and student projects, including setbacks and lessons. The piece argues that early exposure to entrepreneurship shapes students' futures and the wider economy.
one_line: New Horizons Academy's student entrepreneurship program blends curriculum, pitching, mentorship and community support to turn school projects into real-world business experience.
key_facts: On 10 September 2023, New Horizons Academy announced an initiative to combine practical business knowledge with young entrepreneurship.
The program is spearheaded by educator Sarah Johnson and local business mentor Robert Li.
Johnson said at the launch: "It's not just about big ideas... It's about sustainable ideas."
Student projects range from tech start-ups using artificial intelligence for social good to eco-friendly initiatives reducing carbon footprints.
On October 28th, senior Kevin Turner won first place at the school's Young Entrepreneurs' Challenge with a project to streamline community recycling.
The curriculum was adjusted to add basic accounting, digital marketing, and entrepreneurial strategy.
Guest speaker Maya Kapoor visited in November 2023 and ran workshops on strong financial grounding and adaptability in changing markets.
On December 5th, a team of four pitched an app connecting small farmers with local consumers in a mock "Shark Tank"-style session.
Partnerships with local businesses, set up since early 2024, provide internships and mentorship programs for students.
16-year-old Sophia Martinez tested her sustainable clothing line with a local fashion retailer, applying marketing and inventory management skills.
In February 2024, the community initiative "Enterprise Connect" was launched to bring together students, business leaders, and investors.
Councilwoman Angela Richardson said on April 14th: "It takes a village to raise a child, and it takes a community to raise a business."
Alex Newman's food delivery service faced significant challenges with licensing and scalability, teaching him about service-business logistics.
Curricula are continuously updated for technological advances and changing consumer behavior.
